The Ligue 1 season continued to deliver high-stakes drama on May 3, 2026 , as Nice hosted Lens in a match defined by tactical intrigue and moments of individual brilliance. With both sides desperate for points in the final stretch of the campaign, the atmosphere at the stadium was electric from the opening whistle, setting the stage for a physical and unpredictable encounter. A Cagey Opening at the Allianz Riviera The match began with both sides testing each other through set-pieces. Nice looked particularly dangerous early on, with Tom Louchet delivering several teasing corners that kept the Lens backline on high alert. In the 12th minute, a defensive blunder by Pierre Ganiou almost gifted the hosts an opener, but the visitors managed to scramble the ball clear. Juma Bah came closest for the home side in the 17th minute, rising highest to meet a Louchet cross, but his header was comfortably gathered by Robin Risser . Lens responded with pressure of their own, primarily through the delivery of Florian Thauvin , whose corners frequently caused chaos in the Nice penalty area. The game took a brief pause in the 21st minute as the referee consulted VAR for a potential penalty in favor of Nice , though play eventually resumed without a spot-kick being awarded. As the first half progressed, the contest turned increasingly physical; Malang Sarr was booked for unsportsmanlike conduct, and both Juma Bah and Florian Thauvin received yellow cards just before the interval as the intensity boiled over. Saint-Maximin Breaks the Deadlock The second half saw the deadlock finally broken in spectacular fashion. In the 60th minute, Adrien Thomasson found space in the middle of the park and threaded a pass to Allan Saint-Maximin . The mercurial forward, showing the flair that has made him a household name, unleashed a powerful left-footed strike from outside the box that beat the diving Yehvann Diouf to give Lens a 1-0 lead. The goal sparked a frantic response from Nice manager, who opted for a triple substitution in the 71st minute, introducing Ali Abdi , Isak Jansson , and Salis Abdul Samed to find a way back into the game. Lens looked to consolidate their lead, with Odsonne Edouard leading the line effectively before being replaced by Abdallah Sima . However, the momentum shifted dramatically in the 81st minute. Saud Abdulhamid , acting as the last man, committed a professional foul to stop a goal-scoring opportunity and was shown a straight red card. The dismissal left Lens vulnerable and forced them into a defensive shell for the closing stages. Late Drama and the Equalizer Capitalizing on their numerical advantage, Nice poured forward. The pressure told in the 84th minute when a loose ball in the box fell perfectly for the substitute Ali Abdi . The defender reacted quickest, stabbing the ball home with his left foot to send the home crowd into raptures and level the score at 1-1. The final minutes were played at a breakneck pace, with Adrien Thomasson receiving a yellow card for dissent as tensions flared between the players and the officials. In stoppage time, Nice pushed for a winner, with Kevin Carlos nearly connecting with a volley that flew just wide of the target. Melvin Bard was forced into a tactical foul to halt a late Lens counter-attack, earning himself a booking in the process. Despite the frantic end-to-end action and five minutes of added time, neither side could find a decisive third goal. The referee blew the whistle on a hard-fought draw that saw Lens finish with ten men and Nice walking away with a well-earned point thanks to their late resurgence.

Youri Tielemans was active for the visitors, delivering several corners from both flanks, but the Forest backline, marshaled effectively, cleared its lines with ease. The referee initially allowed play to continue during a Nottingham Forest attack, but a signal from the VAR room brought the match to a standstill. Upon reviewing the footage on the pitchside monitor, it was determined that Lucas Digne had handled the ball inside the area. Despite heavy protests from the Villa defender, the official pointed to the spot. Chris Wood stepped up to take the responsibility in the 71st minute. The veteran striker kept his composure under immense pressure, striking the ball with his right foot. While Emiliano Martinez guessed correctly and came agonizingly close to a spectacular save, the power was enough to carry the ball into the net. Holding Firm Against the Villa Surge Facing a deficit, Aston Villa looked to their bench for inspiration, introducing Jadon Sancho , Ian Maatsen , and Douglas Luiz in a triple tactical substitution. The pressure from the visitors intensified, and the game became increasingly physical. Youri Tielemans saw his name go into the referee's book following a rough challenge as frustrations began to boil over. Forest remained dangerous on the break, however, and Neco Williams nearly doubled the lead with a header in the 89th minute, only to be denied by a comfortable save from Emiliano Martinez . As the match entered six minutes of stoppage time, Aston Villa threw everything forward. Jadon Sancho carved out a late chance with a powerful drive from outside the box, but Stefan Ortega stood tall to claim the ball and preserve the clean sheet. Morato and Zach Abbott provided crucial clearances in the dying seconds to repel a flurry of crosses from Tielemans . When the final whistle blew, Nottingham Forest had secured a vital victory, built on defensive resilience and a clinical moment from the penalty spot.
